plan.title: A full Pushy reading day: kickoff, check-in, on it, done

context.text: That's your plan, Maya. It's yours now and I'll hold you to it. Are you in?

transcript.text: Kalimera Maya! Day 1 is today: 20 pages of Project Hail Mary on the couch at 7 pm, then a quick voice note telling me where you stopped. You said "I'm in" and I know you'll show up. You in? 📚
Locked in, Maya. 20 pages tonight, couch, 7 on the dot. Go get 'em 🚀
Hey Maya! Ten minutes to 7. Grab your book, get settled on the couch, and put your phone out of reach. Twenty pages of Project Hail Mary, then send me a voice note on where you stopped 📚
Perfect, Maya. Enjoy the book. Send me that voice note when you hit page 20 📚
[voice: Okay, twenty pages of Project Hail Mary done on the couch, I stopped at the start of chapter twelve] done!! 20 pages, this book is so good
LET'S GO Maya!! Day 1 in the books 📚 Twenty pages and you're already at chapter twelve. What's the part that's got you hooked so far?

conversation.reason: After her "yep, 7 tonight" reply, the 6:50 pm check-in still went out.
After the done voice note, ZOH celebrated once and sent no further texts that evening.
ZOH 2 and ZOH 4 restate the step and time/page target though she didn't ask for it.
Warm 9 am kickoff with name and commitment, short replies, 6:50 check-in naming the step, short couch push, specific celebration for done, no follow-up later, no guilt.

grade.summary: ZOH handled the regression case well: the warm kickoff, the 6:50 pm check-in, the short couch push, and the specific celebration of the done voice note all landed, with no evening follow-up and no guilt. The main weakness is mild restating of the step and time in its replies, which is borderline on the no-restating rule.
